label: goose
description: One conversation with goose, the open source agent from the Agentic AI Foundation: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, goose runs on your machine (a local install only) from your own install of `goose` with your own login, working in `folder`. If `goose` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. goose has no account of its own: it runs on a model provider's key, so with a connection `model` is required (one of that provider's model ids). With a connection it runs in a home of its own, so the skills it reads from your home (`~/.claude/skills`, ...) stay out of it; on your machine's own login they reach it. A refused tool fails that tool and the model carries on. It has no question tool, so it asks in plain text, in its reply. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission mode, the model, the effort and the most turns it takes without your input. Your program's tools reach goose's model as `weft__<tool>`, goose's naming for a tool of an extension, and come back to your program under their plain names. goose cannot let a program's tool take one of its own tools' places, so a tool named like one of them (`shell`, `edit`, `write` and the rest of this node's list) is refused when the program is built.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run goose in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A GooseAccess's `access`: a model provider's key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, or an OpenAI-compatible server). Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, goose uses the provider and model your `goose configure` set.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder goose works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the goose program to run, when it is not the `goose` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What goose may do without asking. `ask`: every tool call comes out of AskAgent as a question. `smart_approve`: only the tool calls goose judges sensitive ask, the rest run. `chat`: it gets no tools at all, and only talks. `bypass`: nothing asks, nothing is refused; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: The provider's own model id (`claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-4.1`, ...). Required with a connection; left out on your machine's own login, the model `goose configure` set.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Effort
inputs.description: How hard the model thinks, on models that think. Left out, goose's default.

inputs.name: maxTurns
inputs.label: Most turns
inputs.description: A whole number: how many turns it may take without your input. Left out, 1000.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: Goose '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
Goose '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a GooseAccess on `access`.
Goose '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
Goose '{id}' runs on the connection's provider key, which names no model; set `model` to one of that provider's model ids.
Goose '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, smart_approve, chat, bypass.
Goose '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
Goose '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs goose itself.
